<file path="Engine/src/main.cpp">
#include "engine.h"
#include "redis_client.h"
#include "kafka_producer.h"
#include "snapshot.h"
#include "json_util.h"

#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
#include <iostream>
#include <csignal>
#include <atomic>
#include <thread>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <chrono>
#include <string>

using nlohmann::json;
using namespace exch;

static std::atomic<bool> running{true};
static Engine* g_engine = nullptr;
static KafkaProducer* g_kafka = nullptr;
static RedisConsumer* g_redis = nullptr;

static void handleSignal(int sig) {
  std::cerr << "[engine] signal received: " << sig << std::endl;
  running.store(false);
}

static std::string envOr(const char* key, const std::string& def) {
  const char* v = std::getenv(key);
  if (v && *v) return v;
  return def;
}

static int envIntOr(const char* key, int def) {
  const char* v = std::getenv(key);
  if (v && *v) return std::atoi(v);
  return def;
}

int main() {
  std::signal(SIGINT, handleSignal);
  std::signal(SIGTERM, handleSignal);
  std::signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN);

  std::string redisHost = envOr("REDIS_HOST", "127.0.0.1");
  int redisPort = envIntOr("REDIS_PORT", 6379);
  std::string stream = envOr("REDIS_STREAM_ORDER_COMMANDS", "order_commands");
  std::string group = envOr("REDIS_CONSUMER_GROUP", "engine-group");
  std::string consumer = envOr("REDIS_CONSUMER_NAME", "engine-1");
  std::string eventsChannel = envOr("REDIS_EVENTS_CHANNEL", "engine_events");
  std::string kafkaBrokers = envOr("KAFKA_BROKERS", "localhost:9092");
  std::string kafkaTopic = envOr("KAFKA_ENGINE_EVENTS_TOPIC", "engine_events");
  std::string snapshotPath = envOr("SNAPSHOT_PATH", "engine_state.json");
  int snapshotInterval = envIntOr("SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_SECONDS", 900);

  RedisConsumer consumerClient;
  if (!consumerClient.client.connect(redisHost, redisPort)) {
    std::cerr << "Cannot connect to Redis at " << redisHost << ":" << redisPort << std::endl;
    return 1;
  }
  if (!consumerClient.ensureGroup(stream, group)) {
    std::cerr << "Cannot ensure consumer group " << group << std::endl;
    return 1;
  }
  g_redis = &consumerClient;

  KafkaProducer producer;
  if (!producer.init(kafkaBrokers)) {
    std::cerr << "Failed to init Kafka producer" << std::endl;
  }
  g_kafka = &producer;

  Engine engine;
  g_engine = &engine;

  engine.setEventCallback([&](const json& ev) {
    std::string s = ev.dump();
    // 1) Publish to Redis Pub/Sub
    consumerClient.publish(eventsChannel, s);
    // 2) Publish to Kafka
    if (ev.contains("market") && ev["market"].is_string()) {
      producer.produce(kafkaTopic, ev["market"].get<std::string>(), s);
    } else {
      producer.produce(kafkaTopic, "global", s);
    }
  });

  SnapshotService snapshots(&engine, snapshotPath, snapshotInterval);
  if (!snapshots.loadLatest()) {
    std::cerr << "[snapshot] no existing snapshot loaded" << std::endl;
  } else {
    std::cerr << "[snapshot] loaded " << snapshotPath << std::endl;
    engine.publishAllBookUpdates();
  }
  snapshots.start();

  std::cerr << "[engine] started; consuming " << stream
            << " group=" << group << " consumer=" << consumer
            << " events_channel=" << eventsChannel << std::endl;

  int loopCount = 0;
  while (running.load()) {
    loopCount++;
    if (loopCount % 10 == 0) {
      std::cerr << "[engine] loop iteration " << loopCount << ", running=" << running.load() << std::endl;
    }
    auto entries = consumerClient.readGroup(stream, group, consumer, 32, 1000);
    for (auto& e : entries) {
      auto j = fieldsToJson(e.fields);
      try {
        engine.processCommand(j);
      } catch (std::exception& ex) {
        std::cerr << "[engine] processCommand error: " << ex.what() << std::endl;
      }
      consumerClient.ack(stream, group, e.id);
    }
  }

  std::cerr << "[engine] shutting down..." << std::endl;
  snapshots.saveNow();
  producer.flush(2000);
  return 0;
}
</file>

<file path="Engine/src/orderbook.cpp">
#include "orderbook.h"
#include <sstream>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <algorithm>
#include <deque>

namespace exch {

const char* orderTypeStr(OrderType t) {
  return t == OrderType::Limit ? "limit" : "market";
}
const char* sideStr(Side s) {
  return s == Side::Buy ? "buy" : "sell";
}
const char* tifStr(TimeInForce t) {
  switch (t) {
    case TimeInForce::GTC: return "GTC";
    case TimeInForce::IOC: return "IOC";
    case TimeInForce::FOK: return "FOK";
  }
  return "GTC";
}
const char* statusStr(OrderStatus s) {
  switch (s) {
    case OrderStatus::Pending: return "pending";
    case OrderStatus::Open: return "open";
    case OrderStatus::PartiallyFilled: return "partially_filled";
    case OrderStatus::Filled: return "filled";
    case OrderStatus::Canceled: return "canceled";
    case OrderStatus::Rejected: return "rejected";
    case OrderStatus::Expired: return "expired";
  }
  return "pending";
}

OrderType parseOrderType(const std::string& s) {
  if (s == "limit") return OrderType::Limit;
  return OrderType::Market;
}
Side parseSide(const std::string& s) {
  if (s == "sell") return Side::Sell;
  return Side::Buy;
}
TimeInForce parseTif(const std::string& s) {
  if (s == "IOC") return TimeInForce::IOC;
  if (s == "FOK") return TimeInForce::FOK;
  return TimeInForce::GTC;
}

OrderBook::OrderBook(std::string market) : market_(std::move(market)) {}

std::map<Decimal, std::deque<std::shared_ptr<Order>>, std::greater<Decimal>>::iterator OrderBook::bestBid() {
  return bids_.begin();
}
std::map<Decimal, std::deque<std::shared_ptr<Order>>>::iterator OrderBook::bestAsk() {
  return asks_.begin();
}

void OrderBook::popFrontOrder(
    std::map<Decimal, std::deque<std::shared_ptr<Order>>, std::greater<Decimal>>& book,
    std::map<Decimal, std::deque<std::shared_ptr<Order>>, std::greater<Decimal>>::iterator& it) {
  // Shared with asks_ via implicit cast
}

std::vector<Trade> OrderBook::match(Order& order) {
  std::vector<Trade> trades;
  if (order.type == OrderType::Limit && order.postOnly) {
    // Reject if would cross.
    if (order.side == Side::Buy) {
      auto it = bestAsk();
      if (it != asks_.end() && it->first <= order.price) {
        order.status = OrderStatus::Rejected;
        return trades;
      }
    } else {
      auto it = bestBid();
      if (it != bids_.end() && it->first >= order.price) {
        order.status = OrderStatus::Rejected;
        return trades;
      }
    }
  }

  // FOK pre-check: must be fully fillable.
  if (order.type == OrderType::Limit && order.tif == TimeInForce::FOK) {
    Decimal remaining = order.quantity;
    if (order.side == Side::Buy) {
      Decimal cumulative;
      for (auto it = asks_.begin(); it != asks_.end() && remaining > Decimal(int64_t(0)); ++it) {
        if (it->first > order.price) break;
        Decimal lvlQty;
        for (auto& o : it->second) {
          lvlQty += o->quantity - o->filled;
        }
        cumulative += lvlQty;
      }
      if (cumulative < order.quantity) {
        order.status = OrderStatus::Rejected;
        return trades;
      }
    } else {
      Decimal cumulative;
      for (auto it = bids_.begin(); it != bids_.end() && remaining > Decimal(int64_t(0)); ++it) {
        if (it->first < order.price) break;
        Decimal lvlQty;
        for (auto& o : it->second) {
          lvlQty += o->quantity - o->filled;
        }
        cumulative += lvlQty;
      }
      if (cumulative < order.quantity) {
        order.status = OrderStatus::Rejected;
        return trades;
      }
    }
  }

  // Matching loop.
  auto tryMatch = [&](Side incomingSide, const Decimal& limitPrice) {
    while (true) {
      Decimal remaining = order.quantity - order.filled;
      if (remaining <= Decimal(int64_t(0))) break;
      if (incomingSide == Side::Buy) {
        auto it = bestAsk();
        if (it == asks_.end()) break;
        if (order.type == OrderType::Limit && it->first > limitPrice) break;
        // Match against this level
        Decimal execPrice = it->first;
        while (remaining > Decimal(int64_t(0)) && !it->second.empty()) {
          auto& front = it->second.front();
          Decimal available = front->quantity - front->filled;
          if (available <= Decimal(int64_t(0))) {
            // Should not happen
            it->second.pop_front();
            orderIndex_.erase(front->id);
            continue;
          }
          Decimal execQty = std::min(remaining, available);
          // Update maker.
          front->filled += execQty;
          if (front->filled >= front->quantity) {
            front->status = OrderStatus::Filled;
          } else {
            front->status = OrderStatus::PartiallyFilled;
          }
          // Update taker.
          order.filled += execQty;
          remaining = order.quantity - order.filled;
          // Emit trade
          Trade tr;
          tr.market = market_;
          tr.makerOrderId = front->id;
          tr.takerOrderId = order.id;
          tr.makerUserId = front->userId;
          tr.takerUserId = order.userId;
          tr.takerSide = Side::Buy;
          tr.price = execPrice;
          tr.quantity = execQty;
          tr.timestamp = order.timestamp;
          trades.push_back(tr);
          if (front->filled >= front->quantity) {
            orderIndex_.erase(front->id);
            it->second.pop_front();
          }
        }
        if (it->second.empty()) asks_.erase(it);
      } else {
        auto it = bestBid();
        if (it == bids_.end()) break;
        if (order.type == OrderType::Limit && it->first < limitPrice) break;
        Decimal execPrice = it->first;
        while (remaining > Decimal(int64_t(0)) && !it->second.empty()) {
          auto& front = it->second.front();
          Decimal available = front->quantity - front->filled;
          if (available <= Decimal(int64_t(0))) {
            it->second.pop_front();
            orderIndex_.erase(front->id);
            continue;
          }
          Decimal execQty = std::min(remaining, available);
          front->filled += execQty;
          if (front->filled >= front->quantity) {
            front->status = OrderStatus::Filled;
          } else {
            front->status = OrderStatus::PartiallyFilled;
          }
          order.filled += execQty;
          remaining = order.quantity - order.filled;
          Trade tr;
          tr.market = market_;
          tr.makerOrderId = front->id;
          tr.takerOrderId = order.id;
          tr.makerUserId = front->userId;
          tr.takerUserId = order.userId;
          tr.takerSide = Side::Sell;
          tr.price = execPrice;
          tr.quantity = execQty;
          tr.timestamp = order.timestamp;
          trades.push_back(tr);
          if (front->filled >= front->quantity) {
            orderIndex_.erase(front->id);
            it->second.pop_front();
          }
        }
        if (it->second.empty()) bids_.erase(it);
      }
    }
  };

  if (order.side == Side::Buy) {
    Decimal limit = (order.type == OrderType::Limit) ? order.price : Decimal(int64_t(1e18));
    tryMatch(Side::Buy, limit);
  } else {
    Decimal limit = (order.type == OrderType::Limit) ? order.price : Decimal(int64_t(0));
    tryMatch(Side::Sell, limit);
  }

  Decimal remaining = order.quantity - order.filled;
  if (remaining > Decimal(int64_t(0))) {
    if (order.type == OrderType::Limit && order.tif == TimeInForce::GTC) {
      // Rest on book
      auto o = std::make_shared<Order>(order);
      o->status = (order.filled > Decimal(int64_t(0))) ? OrderStatus::PartiallyFilled : OrderStatus::Open;
      if (order.side == Side::Buy) {
        bids_[order.price].push_back(o);
      } else {
        asks_[order.price].push_back(o);
      }
      orderIndex_[o->id] = {order.side == Side::Buy, order.price.toString()};
      // Mark order in caller's copy: it now rests with filled amount.
      order.status = o->status;
    } else if (order.tif == TimeInForce::IOC) {
      order.status = (order.filled > Decimal(int64_t(0))) ? OrderStatus::PartiallyFilled : OrderStatus::Canceled;
    } else {
      // FOK was pre-checked; should not reach here.
      order.status = (order.filled > Decimal(int64_t(0))) ? OrderStatus::PartiallyFilled : OrderStatus::Canceled;
    }
  } else {
    order.status = OrderStatus::Filled;
  }
  return trades;
}

bool OrderBook::cancelResting(const std::string& orderId) {
  auto idx = orderIndex_.find(orderId);
  if (idx == orderIndex_.end()) return false;
  bool isBid = idx->second.first;
  const std::string& priceKey = idx->second.second;
  if (isBid) {
    for (auto it = bids_.begin(); it != bids_.end(); ++it) {
      if (it->first.toString() != priceKey) continue;
      auto& q = it->second;
      for (auto oit = q.begin(); oit != q.end(); ++oit) {
        if ((*oit)->id == orderId) {
          (*oit)->status = OrderStatus::Canceled;
          q.erase(oit);
          orderIndex_.erase(idx);
          if (q.empty()) bids_.erase(it);
          return true;
        }
      }
    }
  } else {
    for (auto it = asks_.begin(); it != asks_.end(); ++it) {
      if (it->first.toString() != priceKey) continue;
      auto& q = it->second;
      for (auto oit = q.begin(); oit != q.end(); ++oit) {
        if ((*oit)->id == orderId) {
          (*oit)->status = OrderStatus::Canceled;
          q.erase(oit);
          orderIndex_.erase(idx);
          if (q.empty()) asks_.erase(it);
          return true;
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return false;
}

bool OrderBook::cancel(const std::string& orderId) {
  return cancelResting(orderId);
}

nlohmann::json OrderBook::depthJson(int depth) const {
  nlohmann::json out;
  out["bids"] = nlohmann::json::array();
  out["asks"] = nlohmann::json::array();
  int b = 0;
  for (auto it = bids_.begin(); it != bids_.end() && b < depth; ++it, ++b) {
    Decimal qty;
    for (auto& o : it->second) qty += o->quantity - o->filled;
    out["bids"].push_back({it->first.toString(), qty.toString()});
  }
  int a = 0;
  for (auto it = asks_.begin(); it != asks_.end() && a < depth; ++it, ++a) {
    Decimal qty;
    for (auto& o : it->second) qty += o->quantity - o->filled;
    out["asks"].push_back({it->first.toString(), qty.toString()});
  }
  return out;
}

nlohmann::json OrderBook::serializeState() const {
  nlohmann::json state;
  state["market"] = market_;
  state["bids"] = nlohmann::json::array();
  for (auto& [price, q] : bids_) {
    for (auto& o : q) {
      nlohmann::json oj;
      oj["id"] = o->id;
      oj["userId"] = o->userId;
      oj["side"] = sideStr(o->side);
      oj["type"] = orderTypeStr(o->type);
      oj["price"] = o->price.toString();
      oj["quantity"] = o->quantity.toString();
      oj["filled"] = o->filled.toString();
      oj["tif"] = tifStr(o->tif);
      oj["reduceOnly"] = o->reduceOnly;
      oj["postOnly"] = o->postOnly;
      oj["clientOrderId"] = o->clientOrderId;
      oj["leverage"] = o->leverage.toString();
      oj["marginMode"] = o->marginMode;
      oj["timestamp"] = o->timestamp;
      state["bids"].push_back(oj);
    }
  }
  state["asks"] = nlohmann::json::array();
  for (auto& [price, q] : asks_) {
    for (auto& o : q) {
      nlohmann::json oj;
      oj["id"] = o->id;
      oj["userId"] = o->userId;
      oj["side"] = sideStr(o->side);
      oj["type"] = orderTypeStr(o->type);
      oj["price"] = o->price.toString();
      oj["quantity"] = o->quantity.toString();
      oj["filled"] = o->filled.toString();
      oj["tif"] = tifStr(o->tif);
      oj["reduceOnly"] = o->reduceOnly;
      oj["postOnly"] = o->postOnly;
      oj["clientOrderId"] = o->clientOrderId;
      oj["leverage"] = o->leverage.toString();
      oj["marginMode"] = o->marginMode;
      oj["timestamp"] = o->timestamp;
      state["asks"].push_back(oj);
    }
  }
  return state;
}

void OrderBook::restoreState(const nlohmann::json& state) {
  bids_.clear();
  asks_.clear();
  orderIndex_.clear();
  for (auto& oj : state.value("bids", nlohmann::json::array())) {
    Order o;
    o.id = oj.value("id", "");
    o.userId = oj.value("userId", "");
    o.market = market_;
    o.side = parseSide(oj.value("side", "buy"));
    o.type = parseOrderType(oj.value("type", "limit"));
    o.price = Decimal(oj.value("price", "0"));
    o.quantity = Decimal(oj.value("quantity", "0"));
    o.filled = Decimal(oj.value("filled", "0"));
    o.tif = parseTif(oj.value("tif", "GTC"));
    o.reduceOnly = oj.value("reduceOnly", false);
    o.postOnly = oj.value("postOnly", false);
    o.clientOrderId = oj.value("clientOrderId", "");
    o.leverage = Decimal(oj.value("leverage", "1"));
    o.marginMode = oj.value("marginMode", "isolated");
    o.timestamp = oj.value("timestamp", (int64_t)0);
    o.status = (o.filled >= o.quantity) ? OrderStatus::Filled : OrderStatus::Open;
    auto ptr = std::make_shared<Order>(o);
    bids_[o.price].push_back(ptr);
    orderIndex_[o.id] = {true, o.price.toString()};
  }
  for (auto& oj : state.value("asks", nlohmann::json::array())) {
    Order o;
    o.id = oj.value("id", "");
    o.userId = oj.value("userId", "");
    o.market = market_;
    o.side = parseSide(oj.value("side", "sell"));
    o.type = parseOrderType(oj.value("type", "limit"));
    o.price = Decimal(oj.value("price", "0"));
    o.quantity = Decimal(oj.value("quantity", "0"));
    o.filled = Decimal(oj.value("filled", "0"));
    o.tif = parseTif(oj.value("tif", "GTC"));
    o.reduceOnly = oj.value("reduceOnly", false);
    o.postOnly = oj.value("postOnly", false);
    o.clientOrderId = oj.value("clientOrderId", "");
    o.leverage = Decimal(oj.value("leverage", "1"));
    o.marginMode = oj.value("marginMode", "isolated");
    o.timestamp = oj.value("timestamp", (int64_t)0);
    o.status = (o.filled >= o.quantity) ? OrderStatus::Filled : OrderStatus::Open;
    auto ptr = std::make_shared<Order>(o);
    asks_[o.price].push_back(ptr);
    orderIndex_[o.id] = {false, o.price.toString()};
  }
}

size_t OrderBook::openOrderCount() const {
  size_t c = 0;
  for (auto& [_, q] : bids_) c += q.size();
  for (auto& [_, q] : asks_) c += q.size();
  return c;
}

}  // namespace exch
</file>

#pragma once
#include "decimal.h"
#include <string>
#include <queue>
#include <map>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>
#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

namespace exch {

enum class OrderType { Market, Limit };
enum class Side { Buy, Sell };
enum class TimeInForce { GTC, IOC, FOK };
enum class OrderStatus { Pending, Open, PartiallyFilled, Filled, Canceled, Rejected, Expired };

const char* orderTypeStr(OrderType t);
const char* sideStr(Side s);
const char* tifStr(TimeInForce t);
const char* statusStr(OrderStatus s);
OrderType parseOrderType(const std::string& s);
Side parseSide(const std::string& s);
TimeInForce parseTif(const std::string& s);

struct Order {
  std::string id;
  std::string userId;
  std::string market;
  Side side;
  OrderType type;
  Decimal price;        // valid if type == Limit
  Decimal quantity;
  Decimal filled;       // currently filled quantity
  TimeInForce tif;
  bool reduceOnly;
  bool postOnly;
  std::string clientOrderId;
  Decimal leverage;
  std::string marginMode;
  int64_t timestamp;
  OrderStatus status;
};

struct Trade {
  std::string market;
  std::string makerOrderId;
  std::string takerOrderId;
  std::string makerUserId;
  std::string takerUserId;
  Side takerSide;
  Decimal price;
  Decimal quantity;
  int64_t timestamp;
};

class OrderBook {
public:
  explicit OrderBook(std::string market);

  const std::string& market() const { return market_; }

  // Match an incoming order. Returns a vector of trades executed.
  // The order's `filled` and `status` are updated.
  std::vector<Trade> match(Order& order);

  // Cancel an order. Returns true if found and removed.
  bool cancel(const std::string& orderId);

  // Snapshot top N levels as JSON.
  nlohmann::json depthJson(int depth) const;

  // Serialize full book state (open orders) for snapshot.
  nlohmann::json serializeState() const;

  // Restore from snapshot state.
  void restoreState(const nlohmann::json& state);

  size_t openOrderCount() const;
  size_t bidLevels() const { return bids_.size(); }
  size_t askLevels() const { return asks_.size(); }

private:
  using OrderPtr = std::shared_ptr<Order>;
  using Queue = std::deque<OrderPtr>;

  // Return best bid (highest) iterator or end.
  std::map<Decimal, Queue, std::greater<Decimal>>::iterator bestBid();
  // Return best ask (lowest) iterator or end.
  std::map<Decimal, Queue>::iterator bestAsk();

  // Remove the front order from a queue; if the queue becomes empty, erase the price level.
  void popFrontOrder(std::map<Decimal, Queue, std::greater<Decimal>>& book,
                     std::map<Decimal, Queue, std::greater<Decimal>>::iterator& it);

  // Cancel a single resting order (no trade).
  bool cancelResting(const std::string& orderId);

  std::string market_;
  // price -> FIFO queue
  std::map<Decimal, Queue, std::greater<Decimal>> bids_;
  std::map<Decimal, Queue> asks_;
  std::unordered_map<std::string, std::pair<bool, std::string /*price key*/>> orderIndex_;
  // For faster cancel, track order -> (side bool true=bid, price string).
};

}  // namespace exch

<file path="Engine/src/redis_client.cpp">
#include "redis_client.h"
#include <cstring>
#include <iostream>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <vector>

namespace exch {

RedisClient::RedisClient() = default;
RedisClient::~RedisClient() {
  if (ctx_) {
    redisFree(ctx_);
    ctx_ = nullptr;
  }
}

bool RedisClient::connect(const std::string& host, int port) {
  host_ = host;
  port_ = port;
  if (ctx_) {
    redisFree(ctx_);
    ctx_ = nullptr;
  }
  struct timeval timeout = {2, 0};
  ctx_ = redisConnectWithTimeout(host.c_str(), port, timeout);
  if (!ctx_ || ctx_->err) {
    std::cerr << "Redis connect error: " << (ctx_ ? ctx_->errstr : "unknown") << std::endl;
    if (ctx_) { redisFree(ctx_); ctx_ = nullptr; }
    return false;
  }
  return true;
}

bool RedisClient::isConnected() const { return ctx_ != nullptr && ctx_->err == 0; }

static std::string toStr(redisReply* r) {
  if (!r) return "";
  return std::string(r->str, r->len);
}

// Helper: execute command with reconnection retry using argv
static redisReply* executeWithRetry(RedisClient& client, int argc, const char** argv, const size_t* argvlen) {
  redisReply* r = (redisReply*)redisCommandArgv(client.context(), argc, argv, argvlen);

  if (!r && client.context()->err) {
    // Connection lost, try reconnect once
    if (client.connect(client.host(), client.port())) {
      r = (redisReply*)redisCommandArgv(client.context(), argc, argv, argvlen);
    }
  }
  return r;
}

std::vector<StreamEntry> RedisConsumer::readGroup(
    const std::string& stream,
    const std::string& group,
    const std::string& consumer,
    int count,
    int blockMs) {
  std::vector<StreamEntry> out;
  if (!client.isConnected()) return out;

  std::string countStr = std::to_string(count);
  std::string blockStr = std::to_string(blockMs);

  const char* argv[] = {
    "XREADGROUP", "GROUP", group.c_str(), consumer.c_str(),
    "COUNT", countStr.c_str(),
    "BLOCK", blockStr.c_str(),
    "STREAMS", stream.c_str(), ">"
  };
  const int argc = 11;
  std::vector<size_t> argvlen(argc);
  for (int i = 0; i < argc; ++i) argvlen[i] = strlen(argv[i]);

  redisReply* r = executeWithRetry(client, argc, argv, argvlen.data());

  if (!r) return out;
  if (r->type == REDIS_REPLY_NIL) {
    freeReplyObject(r);
    return out;
  }
  if (r->type != REDIS_REPLY_ARRAY) {
    freeReplyObject(r);
    return out;
  }
  for (size_t i = 0; i < r->elements; ++i) {
    redisReply* streamReply = r->element[i];
    if (streamReply->type != REDIS_REPLY_ARRAY || streamReply->elements < 2) continue;
    redisReply* entries = streamReply->element[1];
    if (entries->type != REDIS_REPLY_ARRAY) continue;
    for (size_t j = 0; j < entries->elements; ++j) {
      redisReply* entry = entries->element[j];
      if (entry->type != REDIS_REPLY_ARRAY || entry->elements < 2) continue;
      StreamEntry se;
      se.id = toStr(entry->element[0]);
      redisReply* kv = entry->element[1];
      if (kv->type == REDIS_REPLY_ARRAY) {
        for (size_t k = 0; k + 1 < kv->elements; k += 2) {
          se.fields.emplace_back(toStr(kv->element[k]), toStr(kv->element[k + 1]));
        }
      }
      out.push_back(std::move(se));
    }
  }
  freeReplyObject(r);
  return out;
}

bool RedisConsumer::ensureGroup(const std::string& stream, const std::string& group) {
  if (!client.isConnected()) return false;
  const char* argv[] = {"XGROUP", "CREATE", stream.c_str(), group.c_str(), "$", "MKSTREAM"};
  const int argc = 6;
  std::vector<size_t> argvlen(argc);
  for (int i = 0; i < argc; ++i) argvlen[i] = strlen(argv[i]);
  redisReply* r = executeWithRetry(client, argc, argv, argvlen.data());
  if (!r) return false;
  bool ok = (r->type == REDIS_REPLY_STATUS || r->type == REDIS_REPLY_INTEGER);
  if (r->type == REDIS_REPLY_ERROR && std::strstr(r->str, "BUSYGROUP") != nullptr) ok = true;
  freeReplyObject(r);
  return ok;
}

bool RedisConsumer::ack(const std::string& stream, const std::string& group, const std::string& id) {
  if (!client.isConnected()) return false;
  const char* argv[] = {"XACK", stream.c_str(), group.c_str(), id.c_str()};
  const int argc = 4;
  std::vector<size_t> argvlen(argc);
  for (int i = 0; i < argc; ++i) argvlen[i] = strlen(argv[i]);
  redisReply* r = executeWithRetry(client, argc, argv, argvlen.data());
  if (!r) return false;
  bool ok = (r->type == REDIS_REPLY_INTEGER);
  freeReplyObject(r);
  return ok;
}

bool RedisConsumer::publish(const std::string& channel, const std::string& message) {
  if (!client.isConnected()) return false;
  const char* argv[] = {"PUBLISH", channel.c_str(), message.c_str()};
  const int argc = 3;
  std::vector<size_t> argvlen(argc);
  for (int i = 0; i < argc; ++i) argvlen[i] = strlen(argv[i]);
  redisReply* r = executeWithRetry(client, argc, argv, argvlen.data());
  if (!r) return false;
  bool ok = (r->type == REDIS_REPLY_INTEGER);
  freeReplyObject(r);
  return ok;
}

}  // namespace exch

<file path="Engine/src/snapshot.cpp">
#include "snapshot.h"
#include <fstream>
#include <iostream>
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>
#include <iomanip>
#include <sstream>

namespace exch {

SnapshotService::SnapshotService(Engine* engine, const std::string& filePath, int intervalSeconds)
  : engine_(engine), filePath_(filePath), intervalSeconds_(intervalSeconds) {}

void SnapshotService::start() {
  if (running_.exchange(true)) return;
  std::thread([this]() { run(); }).detach();
}

void SnapshotService::stop() {
  running_.store(false);
}

bool SnapshotService::saveNow() {
  if (!engine_) return false;
  auto state = engine_->snapshotState();
  std::ofstream out(filePath_, std::ios::trunc);
  if (!out.is_open()) {
    std::cerr << "snapshot open failed: " << filePath_ << std::endl;
    return false;
  }
  out << state.dump();
  out.close();
  return true;
}

bool SnapshotService::loadLatest() {
  std::ifstream in(filePath_);
  if (!in.is_open()) return false;
  std::stringstream ss;
  ss << in.rdbuf();
  std::string content = ss.str();
  if (content.empty()) return false;
  try {
    auto state = nlohmann::json::parse(content);
    engine_->restoreState(state);
    return true;
  } catch (std::exception& e) {
    std::cerr << "snapshot parse error: " << e.what() << std::endl;
    return false;
  }
}

void SnapshotService::run() {
  while (running_.load()) {
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(intervalSeconds_));
    if (!running_.load()) break;
    if (saveNow()) {
      std::cerr << "[snapshot] saved to " << filePath_ << std::endl;
    }
  }
}

}  // namespace exch
</file>

namespace exch {

class SnapshotService {

  void start();
  void stop();

  // Save snapshot now.
  bool saveNow();

  // Load latest snapshot if present.
  bool loadLatest();

private:
  void run();

  Engine* engine_;
  std::string filePath_;
  int intervalSeconds_;
  std::atomic<bool> running_{false};

# CLAUDE.md — Market Maker Service

## 1. ROLE OF THIS DOCUMENT

You are working inside the existing **Perpetual Futures Exchange** project.

Your task is to build a small, reliable, production-oriented **Market Maker Service** inside the `market_maker/` directory.

This service exists for one primary purpose:

> Continuously provide simulated liquidity to the exchange by observing real-time market prices from Binance and placing/maintaining buy and sell orders on our own exchange around that external reference price.

This is **not** intended to be a sophisticated trading system, quantitative trading platform, arbitrage engine, portfolio manager, or high-frequency trading infrastructure.

The objective is to build the **smallest practical service that continuously keeps our exchange's order book populated with realistic bid/ask liquidity**, while being resilient enough to run continuously in production.

---

# 2. ABSOLUTE FILE-SYSTEM AND WRITE-PERMISSION RULE

## THIS RULE IS NON-NEGOTIABLE

The repository contains an existing exchange application.

The new market maker must live exclusively inside:

```text
market_maker/
```

You may:

* Read any file in the entire repository.
* Inspect the entire exchange architecture.
* Inspect existing API routes.
* Inspect existing authentication.
* Inspect existing database schemas.
* Inspect existing order models.
* Inspect existing controllers/services.
* Inspect existing matching-engine behavior.
* Inspect existing Docker configuration.
* Inspect existing environment configuration.
* Inspect existing tests.
* Inspect existing documentation.

However:

> **YOU MAY ONLY CREATE, MODIFY, DELETE, OR OTHERWISE WRITE FILES INSIDE `market_maker/`.**

You MUST NOT modify anything outside `market_maker/`.

You MUST NOT:

* modify the existing API
* modify the C++ matching engine
* modify PostgreSQL schemas
* modify Redis configuration
* modify Kafka configuration
* modify frontend code
* modify existing exchange services
* modify existing authentication
* modify existing order logic
* modify existing Docker Compose files
* modify root package files
* modify workspace configuration
* modify existing `.env` files
* create helper scripts outside `market_maker/`
* create temporary files outside `market_maker/`
* "fix" unrelated exchange code
* refactor unrelated exchange code
* move existing files
* rename existing files
* delete existing files

If something outside `market_maker/` appears broken or incompatible, DO NOT fix it automatically.

Instead:

1. Investigate it.
2. Determine exactly what the market maker needs.
3. Implement the required compatibility logic inside `market_maker/` if possible.
4. If it genuinely cannot be solved without modifying another directory, STOP and clearly report the required change instead of making it.

The existing exchange is the source of truth.

---

# 3. FIRST STEP: UNDERSTAND THE EXISTING EXCHANGE

Before writing code, inspect the existing repository.

Do not assume the exchange API works in a particular way.

Do not hallucinate endpoints.

Do not invent authentication flows.

Do not invent request bodies.

Do not invent response formats.

Read the existing implementation.

Specifically inspect:

```text
server/
engine/
packages/
```

and any other relevant existing directories.

Determine:

1. How users authenticate.
2. How the bot can authenticate.
3. How users receive/deposit simulated funds.
4. How balances are represented.
5. How markets are represented.
6. How market symbols are represented.
7. How orders are created.
8. How orders are cancelled.
9. How open orders are queried.
10. How order status is returned.
11. How positions are queried.

The existing exchange architecture should be treated as authoritative.

The documented exchange architecture uses an Express/TypeScript API, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, and a standalone C++ matching engine. Orders ultimately travel through the exchange's normal order pipeline and the matching engine is responsible for matching orders. Do not bypass this architecture.

---

# 4. PROJECT OBJECTIVE

The Market Maker Service should provide liquidity to one or more exchange markets.

Example:

```text
External reference:

Binance BTC/USDT
        ↓
     $100,000
```

The bot calculates:

```text
Bid: $99,950
Ask: $100,050
```

and places:

```text
BUY  BTC-USDT-PERP
0.001 BTC @ 99,950

SELL BTC-USDT-PERP
0.001 BTC @ 100,050
```

If Binance moves:

```text
$100,000 → $100,100
```

the bot should update its quotes:

```text
BUY  @ $100,050
SELL @ $100,150
```

The exact spread, quantity, refresh interval, and market should be configuration-driven.

---

# 5. CORE PRINCIPLE

The bot is a **liquidity provider**, not a trading simulator that blindly executes:

```text
BUY
SELL
BUY
SELL
BUY
SELL
```

Do NOT implement a naive loop that randomly buys and sells.

Instead, the bot should continuously maintain:

```text
        External Price
             │
             ▼
       Quote Calculation
          /        \
         /          \
        ▼            ▼
      BID            ASK
```

The purpose is to keep resting liquidity on both sides of the exchange order book.

Users trading against the exchange can then consume those orders.

This creates realistic exchange activity.

QUOTE_REFRESH_MS=1000

PRICE_STALE_MS=3000

MAX_POSITION=0.1

MAX_ORDER_SIZE=0.01

HEALTH_PORT=3001
```

Configuration must be validated when the application starts.

If a required configuration value is missing or invalid:

```text
FAIL FAST
```

Do not start an unsafe bot with undefined configuration.

Never log:

* passwords
* API secrets
* JWTs
* authentication tokens

---

# 11. BINANCE MARKET DATA

Create:

```text
src/market/binanceFeed.ts
```

This component connects to Binance's public WebSocket market-data feed.

The exact Binance stream and message format must be verified from the current Binance API documentation or existing compatible implementation before coding.

Do not hallucinate the WebSocket URL or message schema.

The feed should provide the rest of the application with:

```typescript
interface PriceState {
    price: number;
    timestamp: number;
    connected: boolean;
}
```

or an equivalent strongly typed representation.

---

# 12. NO PRICE PERSISTENCE

The bot must NOT store Binance market prices in:

* PostgreSQL
* Redis
* Kafka
* files
* JSON files
* local databases
* external databases

The price is runtime information only.

The bot only needs:

```text
latest price
latest timestamp
connection status
```

When a new Binance price arrives:

```text
replace old price
```

Do not build historical price storage.

Do not build candles.

Do not build OHLCV.

Do not build analytics.

Do not build technical indicators.

---

# 13. PRICE VALIDATION

Never calculate quotes from an invalid price.

Reject/ignore a Binance update if:

* price is missing
* price cannot be parsed
* price <= 0
* timestamp is invalid
* data is clearly malformed

Never place an order using:

```text
0
NaN
Infinity
undefined
null
stale price
```

---

# 14. STALE PRICE PROTECTION

This is mandatory.

Maintain:

```text
lastPriceUpdateTimestamp
```

If:

```text
currentTime - lastPriceUpdateTimestamp > PRICE_STALE_MS
```

the bot must immediately enter:

```text
QUOTING PAUSED
```

state.

While price data is stale:

* DO NOT place new orders.
* DO NOT update quotes using stale data.
* Preferably cancel active market-making orders to avoid stale liquidity.
* Attempt to reconnect to Binance.
* Resume only after a fresh valid price is received.

Expected lifecycle:

```text
Binance connected
      ↓
Fresh price
      ↓
QUOTING
      ↓
WebSocket disconnected
      ↓
PRICE STALE
      ↓
CANCEL ACTIVE QUOTES
      ↓
RECONNECT
      ↓
Fresh price received
      ↓
QUOTING RESUMED
```

---

# 15. BINANCE RECONNECTION

The Binance WebSocket must automatically reconnect.

Use exponential backoff.

Example:

```text
1 second
2 seconds
4 seconds
8 seconds
16 seconds
30 seconds
30 seconds
...
```

Do not create an infinite rapid reconnect loop.

On successful reconnection:

```text
reset retry counter
```

The service itself must remain alive even if Binance is temporarily unavailable.

A temporary external dependency failure must not crash the process.

---

# 16. QUOTE STRATEGY

Create:

```text
src/strategy/marketMaker.ts
```

The strategy should remain intentionally simple.

Inputs:

```text
reference price
spread
order quantity
tick size
step size
```

Output:

```text
desired bid
desired ask
quantity
```

For example:

```text
Reference:
100,000

Spread:
0.10%

Bid:
99,950

Ask:
100,050
```

The strategy should be deterministic.

Given the same inputs, it should produce the same quotes.

---

# 17. SPREAD

Use configuration:

```env
SPREAD_BPS=10
```

Interpret this correctly as basis points.

Do not hardcode:

```text
0.1%
```

inside multiple places.

The strategy should calculate:

```text
bid = reference price - spread
ask = reference price + spread
```

The exact mathematical implementation should be written clearly and tested.

---

# 18. TICK-SIZE ROUNDING

The exchange market defines:

```text
tick_size
step_size
min_order_size
max_order_size
```

The bot MUST respect these constraints.

Before submitting an order:

```text
calculate price
      ↓
round to tick size
      ↓
validate
      ↓
calculate quantity
      ↓
round to step size
      ↓
validate
      ↓
submit
```

Never send arbitrary floating-point precision to the exchange.

Prefer decimal-safe arithmetic.

Avoid relying on naive JavaScript floating-point calculations for financial values when precision matters.

If the existing exchange API represents financial values as strings, preserve that convention.

---

# 19. QUANTITY

For the MVP, use a fixed configured quantity:

```env
ORDER_SIZE=0.001
```

Do not implement sophisticated dynamic sizing.

However, validate the quantity against:

```text
min_order_size
max_order_size
step_size
```

If the configured quantity is invalid:

```text
fail startup
```

or refuse to quote that market.

Do not continuously send rejected orders.

---

# 20. ORDER MANAGER

Create:

```text
src/orders/orderManager.ts
```

The order manager is responsible for maintaining the desired bid and ask.

Runtime state can look like:

```typescript
interface ActiveOrders {
    bid?: {
        id: string;
        price: string;
        quantity: string;
    };

    ask?: {
        id: string;
        price: string;
        quantity: string;
    };
}
```

This state is ephemeral.

---

# 21. BASIC ORDER MANAGEMENT

At any point, the bot ideally maintains:

```text
ONE BID
ONE ASK
```

for the configured market.

Do not create hundreds of orders.

Do not create duplicate quotes.

Do not continuously place new orders without cancelling/reconciling old ones.

---

# 22. QUOTE REFRESH LOOP

The bot should have a controlled quote refresh interval.

Example:

```env
QUOTE_REFRESH_MS=1000
```

This does NOT mean Binance price is sampled only once per second.

Binance can update continuously.

Instead:

```text
Binance WebSocket
       │
       ▼
latestPrice
       │
       ▼
quote refresh loop
       │
       ▼
calculate desired quotes
       │
       ▼
compare against active orders
```

This prevents excessive API requests.

Do not create an order operation for every market-data tick.

---

# 23. QUOTE REPLACEMENT

Suppose the current orders are:

```text
BUY  @ 99,950
SELL @ 100,050
```

New desired quotes:

```text
BUY  @ 100,000
SELL @ 100,100
```

The order manager should determine that the existing orders are no longer appropriate.

Then:

```text
cancel old bid
cancel old ask
place new bid
place new ask
```

However, implement this carefully.

Avoid unnecessary cancellation if the desired price and quantity are effectively unchanged.

---

# 24. MINIMUM-CHANGE PRINCIPLE

The bot should not touch orders unless necessary.

If:

```text
current bid = desired bid
current ask = desired ask
```

do nothing.

If only the bid changed:

```text
cancel/replace bid
```

without unnecessarily replacing the ask.

This reduces:

* API traffic
* exchange load
* rate-limit risk
* unnecessary order churn

---

# 25. ORDER IDENTIFICATION

Use client order IDs if the exchange API supports them.

Client order IDs should be:

* unique
* deterministic enough for debugging
* generated safely
* associated with the bot

Example conceptual format:

```text
MM-BTC-BID-<unique-id>
MM-BTC-ASK-<unique-id>
```

Do not assume the exchange accepts a particular format until the existing API implementation is inspected.

---

# 26. IDEMPOTENCY

The bot must protect against duplicate order creation.

If a request times out, do NOT blindly assume the order failed.

Possible situation:

```text
Bot → Exchange
       │
       │ order created
       ▼
Exchange
       X
network response lost
       │
       ▼
Bot sees timeout
```

If the bot blindly retries:

```text
order A created
order B created
```

you may accidentally create duplicate liquidity.

The order manager should reconcile with the exchange's actual open-order state before blindly retrying ambiguous order creation.

Use the exchange's existing idempotency/client-order-ID mechanism if available.

---

# 27. EXCHANGE CLIENT

Create:

```text
src/exchange/exchangeClient.ts
```

This should be the ONLY component that knows how to communicate with the exchange REST API.

The strategy must not make HTTP requests.

The Binance feed must not make exchange requests.

The order manager should call methods on `ExchangeClient`.

Example interface:

```typescript
class ExchangeClient {
    authenticate(): Promise<void>;

    getMarket(symbol: string): Promise<Market>;

    getOpenOrders(symbol: string): Promise<Order[]>;

    placeLimitOrder(params: PlaceOrderParams): Promise<Order>;

    cancelOrder(orderId: string): Promise<void>;

    cancelAllOrders(symbol: string): Promise<void>;

    getBalances(): Promise<Balance[]>;

    getPosition(symbol: string): Promise<Position | null>;
}
```

The exact methods and endpoint paths MUST be based on the actual exchange implementation.

Do not invent them.

---

# 28. AUTHENTICATION

The market maker should use a dedicated exchange account.

Prefer:

```text
Market Maker User
```

with sufficient simulated funds.

The bot should use the same legitimate exchange API flow as a normal client wherever possible.

Do not modify the exchange to create a secret bypass.

Do not insert orders directly into:

* PostgreSQL
* Redis
* C++
* Kafka

The bot should place orders through the existing exchange API.

---

# 29. FUNDING / ADDING SIMULATED FUNDS

The bot may need initial balances.

Inspect the existing exchange implementation to determine how deposits or simulated balances work.

If an existing API supports simulated deposits, expose the corresponding operation through:

```text
ExchangeClient
```

and use it only during explicit initialization/setup if necessary.

Do not continuously add funds.

Do not artificially increase funds every trading cycle.

Do not hide losses by repeatedly minting money.

For example:

```text
INITIALIZATION
     ↓
ensure bot has required simulated balance
     ↓
start market making
```

The exact implementation must follow the existing exchange API.

---

# 30. INVENTORY / POSITION PROTECTION

Even though this is a minimal market maker, it must not accumulate unlimited exposure.

Maintain a configured limit:

```env
MAX_POSITION=0.1
```

Before placing new orders, inspect the current position if necessary.

Basic behavior:

```text
Position too long
      ↓
reduce/disable additional BUY liquidity
      ↓
continue SELL liquidity
```

and:

```text
Position too short
      ↓
reduce/disable additional SELL liquidity
      ↓
continue BUY liquidity
```

For the first version, do not build an advanced inventory optimization algorithm.

A simple hard limit is sufficient.

---

# 31. ABSOLUTE POSITION SAFETY

If:

```text
abs(position) >= MAX_POSITION
```

the bot MUST NOT continue increasing exposure in that direction.

It may:

* stop quoting that side
* quote only the reducing side
* cancel orders that would increase exposure

The exact implementation should be simple and deterministic.

---

# 32. EXCHANGE FAILURE HANDLING

The exchange API may fail.

Examples:

```text
connection refused
timeout
500
502
503
429
network error
```

Do not crash the process.

Handle recoverable errors.

Use bounded exponential backoff.

Do not hammer a failing exchange.

Example:

```text
request failed
     ↓
classify error
     ↓
retry if safe
     ↓
backoff
     ↓
reconcile
     ↓
continue
```

---

# 33. RATE LIMIT PROTECTION

Never create an uncontrolled request loop.

The bot must have explicit control over:

* quote refresh frequency
* retry frequency
* cancellation frequency
* order placement frequency

Do not allow a Binance WebSocket burst to produce an equivalent burst of REST calls.

A simple quote scheduler is preferred.

---

# 34. DO NOT OVER-OPTIMIZE FOR HFT

This is not a real high-frequency trading system.

Do not introduce:

* native C++
* kernel bypass
* shared memory
* FIX
* FPGA
* nanosecond timing
* lock-free queues
* custom network stacks

The goal is realistic simulated liquidity.

A controlled refresh interval is more important than microsecond latency.

---

# 35. STATE MACHINE

Implement an explicit conceptual runtime state.

Possible states:

```text
STARTING
CONNECTING
READY
QUOTING
PAUSED
RECONNECTING
STOPPING
STOPPED
```

Example:

```text
STARTING
   ↓
CONNECTING
   ↓
READY
   ↓
QUOTING
```

If Binance disconnects:

```text
QUOTING
   ↓
PAUSED
   ↓
RECONNECTING
```

After fresh price:

```text
RECONNECTING
   ↓
READY
   ↓
QUOTING
```

If the process receives SIGTERM:

```text
QUOTING
   ↓
STOPPING
   ↓
STOPPED
```

Do not make the implementation unnecessarily complicated, but preserve these safety semantics.

---

# 36. GRACEFUL SHUTDOWN

This is mandatory.

Handle:

```text
SIGINT
SIGTERM
```

Shutdown procedure:

```text
STOP NEW QUOTE OPERATIONS
        ↓
CANCEL ACTIVE BOT ORDERS
        ↓
CLOSE BINANCE WEBSOCKET
        ↓
STOP HTTP SERVER
        ↓
EXIT CLEANLY
```

Do not abruptly terminate while leaving stale market-making orders active if the API allows cancellation.

---

# 37. CRASH RECOVERY

The service should be safe to restart.

On startup:

```text
START
 ↓
AUTHENTICATE
 ↓
GET MARKET
 ↓
GET OPEN BOT ORDERS
 ↓
CANCEL/RECONCILE STALE ORDERS
 ↓
WAIT FOR FRESH BINANCE PRICE
 ↓
CALCULATE QUOTES
 ↓
START MARKET MAKING
```

Do not assume in-memory state survived a crash.

The exchange is the source of truth for existing orders.

---

# 38. STARTUP ORDER RECONCILIATION

This is important.

Suppose the bot crashed while these orders existed:

```text
BUY  @ 99,950
SELL @ 100,050
```

After restart, its memory is empty.

It must not simply place another pair.

It should first query the exchange:

```text
GET open orders
```

identify its own orders, and clean up or reconcile them.

Then establish the new desired quotes.

---

# 39. ONLY MANAGE BOT ORDERS

When querying open orders, never cancel unrelated user orders.

The bot must be able to distinguish:

```text
BOT ORDER
```

from:

```text
NORMAL USER ORDER
```

Use whatever identifier is supported by the existing exchange API:

* user account
* client order ID
* metadata
* dedicated bot account

The safest architecture is a dedicated bot exchange account.

---

# 40. HEALTH SERVER

Create:

```text
src/health/healthServer.ts
```

Expose:

```text
GET /health
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "service": "market-maker",
  "binanceConnected": true,
  "exchangeConnected": true,
  "priceFresh": true,
  "quoting": true,
  "market": "BTC-USDT-PERP",
  "activeBid": true,
  "activeAsk": true
}
```

Do not expose:

* passwords
* tokens
* secrets
* private credentials

---

# 41. HEALTH SEMANTICS

The process being alive does not necessarily mean the bot is healthy.

For example:

```text
Node process alive
BUT
Binance disconnected
```

The health status should reflect this.

At minimum distinguish:

```text
process alive
```

from:

```text
market maker actively quoting
```

This allows deployment infrastructure to detect degraded conditions.

---

# 42. LOGGING

Use structured, useful logs.

Examples:

```text
INFO Binance connected
INFO Exchange authentication successful
INFO Market loaded
INFO Initial quote calculated
INFO Bid placed
INFO Ask placed
INFO Quote updated
INFO Order filled
WARN Binance connection lost
WARN Price became stale
WARN Quoting paused
INFO Binance reconnected
INFO Quoting resumed
ERROR Exchange request failed
```

Never log secrets.

Never print complete authentication headers.

Avoid printing every Binance tick.

Do not generate enormous logs at high frequency.

---

# 43. ORDER/FILL MONITORING

The bot should periodically reconcile its orders with the exchange.

Do not rely exclusively on local memory.

For example:

```text
Every N seconds:
    fetch bot open orders
    compare with local state
    reconcile differences
```

If an order disappeared because it was:

* filled
* cancelled
* rejected
* expired

the bot should recognize this.

This allows it to replace liquidity when appropriate.

---

# 44. WHEN A QUOTE IS FILLED

Suppose:

```text
ASK filled
```

The bot should detect that the ask no longer exists.

Then:

```text
refresh position
      ↓
calculate new quotes
      ↓
place replacement liquidity
```

Do not assume that a resting order remains forever.

---

# 45. TRADE ACTIVITY IS THE GOAL

The service exists to produce realistic exchange activity.

Desired behavior:

```text
Binance price moves
        ↓
Bot quotes change
        ↓
Users see liquidity
        ↓
Users place orders
        ↓
Orders match
        ↓
Trades occur
        ↓
Positions update
        ↓
Balances update
        ↓
Order book continues moving
```

The bot should not attempt to manufacture fake fills against itself.

Its purpose is to provide liquidity that other exchange users can interact with.

---

# 46. IMPORTANT: NO SELF-TRADING

The bot should place resting bid/ask orders around the reference price.

It must NOT intentionally cross its own orders.

Do not implement:

```text
bot buys its own sell
```

or:

```text
bot sells into its own bid
```

The bot should provide liquidity, not generate meaningless self-trades.

---

# 47. SIMPLE QUOTING MODEL

For v1, use:

```text
Reference Price = Binance price

Bid = Reference Price - configured spread

Ask = Reference Price + configured spread
```

Then:

```text
round bid to tick size
round ask to tick size
```

and validate:

```text
bid < ask
```

If rounding causes:

```text
bid >= ask
```

do not place orders.

Recalculate using safe spacing.

---

# 48. OPTIONAL FUTURE EXTENSIONS

Do NOT implement these unless explicitly requested later:

* multiple price levels
* dynamic spreads
* volatility-based spreads
* inventory skew
* order-book imbalance
* Binance order-book arbitrage
* multiple external exchanges
* funding-rate strategies
* statistical arbitrage
* technical indicators
* strategy plugins
* machine learning
* historical database
* backtesting
* PnL analytics
* portfolio optimization

The first version should remain intentionally small.

---

# 49. ERROR CLASSIFICATION

Errors should be classified conceptually into:

```text
TRANSIENT
PERMANENT
SAFETY
UNKNOWN
```

Examples:

Transient:

```text
timeout
temporary network error
502
503
```

Permanent/configuration:

```text
invalid market
invalid credentials
invalid quantity
invalid configuration
```

Safety:

```text
stale price
position limit exceeded
invalid market data
```

Unknown:

```text
unexpected API response
```

Safety errors should generally pause quoting rather than blindly retry.

---

# 50. NEVER BLINDLY RETRY ORDERS

This rule is especially important.

A failed network response does NOT necessarily mean an order was not created.

Before retrying an ambiguous order operation:

```text
reconcile with exchange
```

Use client order IDs if available.

Never create duplicate orders because of a timeout.

---

# 51. CONCURRENCY CONTROL

Prevent multiple quote updates from running simultaneously.

Bad:

```text
quote update #1
      ↓
cancel
      ↓
quote update #2
      ↓
cancel
      ↓
quote update #3
```

while previous operations are still executing.

Use a simple serialized order-management mechanism.

Only one order reconciliation cycle should modify the bot's orders at a time.

This is more important than raw speed.

---

# 52. QUOTE LOOP DESIGN

Use a controlled loop such as:

```text
while running:

    wait for next quote interval

    if price is stale:
        pause
        continue

    get latest price

    calculate desired bid/ask

    validate prices and quantity

    check risk

    reconcile current orders

    place/cancel only what is necessary
```

Do not use:

```text
while(true) {
    // immediately execute again
}
```

without controlled scheduling.

---

# 53. NO MEMORY LEAKS

The service is expected to run continuously.

Avoid:

* unbounded arrays
* accumulating WebSocket messages
* storing every price
* storing every order
* storing every fill
* creating unlimited timers
* creating duplicate WebSocket listeners
* creating duplicate event handlers on reconnect

The runtime state should remain bounded.

---

# 54. WEBSOCKET LISTENER MANAGEMENT

When reconnecting to Binance:

* clean up the previous socket
* remove obsolete listeners
* create exactly one active connection
* avoid duplicate price handlers

A reconnect must not result in:

```text
1 connection
2 handlers

then:

1 connection
4 handlers

then:

1 connection
8 handlers
```

This can create duplicate processing and memory leaks.

---

# 55. HTTP CLIENT TIMEOUTS

Every exchange HTTP request must have a timeout.

Never allow:

```text
await request()
```

to hang indefinitely.

Use a reasonable timeout and classify the timeout as a transient failure.

---

# 56. API RESPONSE VALIDATION

Do not blindly trust exchange API responses.

Validate:

* HTTP status
* JSON shape
* order ID
* order status
* price
* quantity

If the API returns an unexpected response, log a useful error and stop unsafe processing.

Do not continue with undefined order IDs.

---

# 57. SECURITY

Do not hardcode:

```text
passwords
tokens
API keys
secrets
JWTs
```

Use environment variables.

Do not commit `.env`.

Provide:

```text
.env.example
```

with placeholders only.

---

# 58. DOCKER

Create:

```text
market_maker/Dockerfile
```

The service should be independently containerizable.

Do not modify the repository's existing Docker configuration.

The Dockerfile must only build/run the market maker.

The service should receive:

```text
EXCHANGE_API_URL
BINANCE_SYMBOL
MARKET
SPREAD_BPS
ORDER_SIZE
...
```

through environment variables.

---

# 59. PROCESS RESILIENCE

The application itself should not terminate because:

* Binance disconnects
* exchange temporarily becomes unavailable
* an order request times out
* one quote calculation fails
* one order gets rejected
* one API request returns malformed data

Only unrecoverable startup/configuration failures should normally terminate the process.

Runtime failures should transition the service into a safe state and recover.

---

# 60. SAFE FAILURE PRINCIPLE

Whenever uncertain:

> Prefer no liquidity over incorrect liquidity.

Examples:

If Binance price is stale:

```text
STOP QUOTING
```

If market metadata is unknown:

```text
STOP QUOTING
```

If position limit is exceeded:

```text
STOP INCREASING EXPOSURE
```

If exchange state is unknown:

```text
RECONCILE FIRST
```

If order creation result is ambiguous:

```text
RECONCILE FIRST
```

Do not guess.

---

Before considering the service complete, test:

### Binance

* connection
* price reception
* malformed data
* disconnect
* reconnect
* stale price detection

### Exchange

* authentication
* market retrieval
* balance retrieval
* order placement
* order cancellation
* open-order retrieval
* position retrieval
* API timeout
* API error

### Strategy

* correct bid
* correct ask
* spread calculation
* tick-size rounding
* step-size rounding
* invalid values

### Order Manager

* first quote
* unchanged quote
* changed quote
* bid-only change
* ask-only change
* filled order
* cancelled order
* duplicate prevention
* restart reconciliation

### Risk

* normal position
* maximum position
* long limit
* short limit
* invalid quantity

### Shutdown

* SIGINT
* SIGTERM
* active order cancellation
* Binance socket cleanup

---

# 62. DO NOT MODIFY EXCHANGE CODE TO MAKE TESTING EASIER

If a test fails because of an existing exchange implementation:

Do NOT modify the exchange.

Investigate the existing implementation and adapt the Market Maker client accordingly.

Only report an external change as necessary if there is genuinely no way to complete the market maker without it.

Create:

market_maker/README.md
```

It must explain:

# 64. IMPLEMENTATION PROCESS

Follow this exact process.

## STEP 1 — READ FIRST

Before writing anything:

```text
Inspect entire exchange repository.
```

Understand the real implementation.

Do not code from assumptions.

## STEP 2 — MAP THE EXCHANGE API

Identify the actual:

```text
authentication endpoint
market endpoint
balance endpoint
order endpoint
cancel endpoint
open-order endpoint
position endpoint
deposit/funding endpoint
```

Document the actual endpoints inside the Market Maker README.

## STEP 3 — DESIGN

Confirm the minimal architecture:

```text
BinanceFeed
     ↓
MarketMaker
     ↓
OrderManager
     ↓
ExchangeClient
```

plus:

```text
RiskManager
HealthServer
```

## STEP 4 — IMPLEMENT BINANCE FEED

Get real-time Binance price working.

Do not connect the strategy yet.

## STEP 5 — IMPLEMENT EXCHANGE CLIENT

Prove the bot can:

```text
authenticate
read market
read balance
place order
read order
cancel order
read position
```

## STEP 6 — IMPLEMENT STRATEGY

Given:

```text
Binance price
```

produce:

```text
bid
ask
```

## STEP 7 — IMPLEMENT ORDER MANAGER

Maintain:

```text
one bid
one ask
```

and safely replace them when needed.

## STEP 8 — ADD SAFETY

Implement:

```text
stale price
reconnect
timeouts
retries
rate limits
position limits
startup reconciliation
graceful shutdown
```

## STEP 9 — HEALTH

Add:

```text
GET /health
```

## STEP 10 — DOCKER

Create the Dockerfile.

## STEP 11 — TEST

Run the complete service against the existing exchange.

---

# 65. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

The Market Maker is complete only when:

### Architecture

* Node.js service exists inside `market_maker/`.
* TypeScript is used.
* Express is used for the service/health endpoint.
* No files outside `market_maker/` were modified.
* No new database is required.

### Binance

* Binance WebSocket connects.
* Real-time prices are received.
* Prices are held only in memory.
* Reconnection works.
* Stale prices pause quoting.

### Exchange

* Bot authenticates successfully.
* Bot can obtain market information.
* Bot can obtain balances.
* Bot can place orders.
* Bot can cancel orders.
* Bot can inspect open orders.
* Bot can inspect its position.

### Liquidity

The exchange order book should show:

```text
BID
ASK
```

around the Binance reference price.

When Binance moves, the bot should update the quotes.

### Reliability

* Runtime exceptions do not unnecessarily kill the process.
* HTTP requests have timeouts.
* Retry behavior is bounded.
* WebSocket reconnection is safe.
* No duplicate WebSocket listeners.
* No uncontrolled request loops.
* No duplicate orders from ambiguous retries.
* Startup reconciliation works.
* Graceful shutdown works.
* Health endpoint works.

### Safety

* No orders from stale prices.
* No orders with invalid quantities.
* No orders outside configured risk limits.
* No intentional self-trading.
* No infinite exposure.
* No secrets in source code.

---

# 66. IMPORTANT DESIGN PHILOSOPHY

Do NOT over-engineer this service.

The exchange is the complicated system.

The Market Maker should remain a small external client.

The final relationship should be:

```text
                 EXTERNAL MARKET
                      Binance
                         │
                         │ price
                         ▼
                 MARKET MAKER BOT
                         │
                         │ orders
                         ▼
                  EXCHANGE REST API
                         │
                         ▼
                  MATCHING ENGINE
                         │
                         ▼
                    ORDER BOOK
                         │
                         ▼
                    EXCHANGE USERS
```

The Market Maker does not replace the exchange.

It does not bypass the exchange.

It does not maintain another copy of the exchange.

It does not become another trading platform.

It simply provides liquidity.

---

# 67. FINAL RULE: DO NOT HALLUCINATE

This rule is extremely important.

Before implementing anything that interacts with the exchange:

> READ THE ACTUAL CODE.

Do not assume:

```text
endpoint names
request bodies
response bodies
authentication format
order status values
market symbols
balance behavior
position behavior
```

If the documentation and implementation disagree:

> The actual implementation is the source of truth.

If something is ambiguous:

> Investigate before coding.

If something cannot be verified:

> Say so instead of inventing it.

---

# 68. FINAL RULE: DO NOT EXPAND SCOPE

The requested product is:

> A minimal, reliable, continuously running market-making service that uses Binance as an external price reference and provides bid/ask liquidity on our existing perpetual futures exchange.

Do not turn this into:

* an algorithmic trading platform
* an arbitrage engine
* a quantitative research system
* a portfolio manager
* a trading framework
* a second exchange
* a database-backed analytics service

Keep it small.

Keep it understandable.

Keep it reliable.

Keep all changes strictly inside:

```text
market_maker/
```

---

# 69. FINAL EXPECTED RESULT

After implementation, running:

```bash
npm run start
```

should produce something conceptually similar to:

```text
[INFO] Market Maker starting
[INFO] Configuration loaded
[INFO] Authenticating with exchange
[INFO] Exchange authentication successful
[INFO] Loading BTC-USDT-PERP market
[INFO] Binance WebSocket connecting
[INFO] Binance connected
[INFO] Current BTC price: 100000.00
[INFO] Calculated bid: 99950.00
[INFO] Calculated ask: 100050.00
[INFO] Bid placed: <order-id>
[INFO] Ask placed: <order-id>
[INFO] Market maker quoting BTC-USDT-PERP
```

When Binance moves:

```text
[INFO] BTC price: 100100.00
[INFO] Desired bid changed
[INFO] Desired ask changed
[INFO] Replacing quotes
[INFO] New bid placed
[INFO] New ask placed
```

If Binance disconnects:

```text
[WARN] Binance connection lost
[WARN] Price is stale
[WARN] Quoting paused
[INFO] Cancelling active quotes
[INFO] Reconnecting to Binance
```

After recovery:

```text
[INFO] Binance reconnected
[INFO] Fresh price received
[INFO] Quoting resumed
```

The service should be able to run continuously for long periods without accumulating state, leaking resources, creating duplicate orders, or requiring manual intervention.

---

# 70. YOUR IMPLEMENTATION PRIORITY

Always prioritize in this order:

```text
1. Correctness
2. Safety
3. Reliability
4. Simplicity
5. Maintainability
6. Performance
```

Do NOT sacrifice correctness or safety merely to make the bot quote faster.

For this project, a stable 500ms–1s quote cycle is more valuable than an unnecessarily complex high-frequency implementation.

The goal is not to win a latency competition.

The goal is to make the exchange **look and behave like an active trading venue with continuously available liquidity**, using Binance as the external price reference.

<file path="Server/src/db/client.ts">
import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/node-postgres";
import { Pool } from "pg";
import * as schema from "./schema";

export const pool = new Pool({
  connectionString:
    process.env.DATABASE_URL ||
    "postgres://param@localhost:5432/exchange",
  max: 20,
});

pool.on("error", (err) => {
  console.error("Unexpected pg pool error", err);
});

export const db = drizzle(pool, { schema });
export { schema };
</file>

  "rejected",

  "closed",
  "liquidated",

// users
export const users = pgTable("users", {
  id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
  email: varchar("email", { length: 255 }).notNull().unique(),

<file path="Server/src/middleware/auth.ts">
import { Request, Response, NextFunction } from "express";
import jwt from "jsonwebtoken";
import { config } from "../config";

export interface AuthPayload {
  userId: string;
  email: string;
  role: "user" | "admin";
}

declare global {
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-namespace
  namespace Express {
    interface Request {
      user?: AuthPayload;
    }
  }
}

export function signToken(payload: AuthPayload): string {
  return jwt.sign(payload, config.jwtSecret, { expiresIn: config.jwtExpiresIn } as jwt.SignOptions);
}

export function verifyToken(token: string): AuthPayload {
  return jwt.verify(token, config.jwtSecret) as AuthPayload;
}

export function authRequired(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
  const header = req.headers.authorization;
  if (!header || !header.startsWith("Bearer ")) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "missing_or_invalid_authorization" });
    return;
  }
  const token = header.slice("Bearer ".length).trim();
  try {
    req.user = verifyToken(token);
    next();
  } catch (e) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "invalid_token" });
  }
}

export function adminRequired(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction): void {
  if (req.user?.role !== "admin") {
    res.status(403).json({ error: "admin_required" });
    return;
  }
  next();
}

<file path="Server/src/routes/auth.ts">
import { Router, Request, Response } from "express";
import { z } from "zod";
import { authRequired } from "../middleware/auth";
import { getUserById, loginUser, registerUser } from "../services/authService";

export const authRouter = Router();

const credsSchema = z.object({
  email: z.string().email(),
  password: z.string().min(6).max(128),
  name: z.string().min(1).max(128).optional(),
});

authRouter.post("/register", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  const parsed = credsSchema.safeParse(req.body);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    res.status(400).json({ error: "validation_error", issues: parsed.error.issues });
    return;
  }
  const { email, password, name } = parsed.data;
  if (!name) {
    res.status(400).json({ error: "name_required" });
    return;
  }
  try {
    const result = await registerUser({ email, password, name });
    res.status(201).json(result);
  } catch (e: unknown) {
    const err = e as { status?: number; message?: string };
    res.status(err.status ?? 500).json({ error: err.message ?? "internal_error" });
  }
});

authRouter.post("/login", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  const parsed = credsSchema
    .pick({ email: true, password: true })
    .safeParse(req.body);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    res.status(400).json({ error: "validation_error", issues: parsed.error.issues });
    return;
  }
  try {
    const result = await loginUser(parsed.data);
    res.json(result);
  } catch (e: unknown) {
    const err = e as { status?: number; message?: string };
    res.status(err.status ?? 500).json({ error: err.message ?? "internal_error" });
  }
});

authRouter.get("/me", authRequired, async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!req.user) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "unauthorized" });
    return;
  }
  const user = await getUserById(req.user.userId);
  if (!user) {
    res.status(404).json({ error: "not_found" });
    return;
  }
  res.json(user);
});

authRouter.post("/logout", authRequired, (_req: Request, res: Response) => {
  // With stateless JWT, logout is client-side. Endpoint provided for completeness.
  res.json({ ok: true });
});

import { Router, Request, Response } from "express";
import { desc, eq, or } from "drizzle-orm";
import { db } from "../db/client";
import { fills } from "../db/schema";
import { authRequired } from "../middleware/auth";

export const fillsRouter = Router();
fillsRouter.use(authRequired);

fillsRouter.get("/", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!req.user) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "unauthorized" });
    return;
  }
  const userId = req.user.userId;
  const rows = await db
    .select()
    .from(fills)
    .where(or(eq(fills.makerUserId, userId), eq(fills.takerUserId, userId)))
    .orderBy(desc(fills.createdAt))
    .limit(parseInt((req.query.limit as string) || "100", 10));
  res.json({ fills: rows });
});

import { Router, Request, Response } from "express";
import { z } from "zod";
import { authRequired } from "../middleware/auth";
import {
  cancelAllOpenOrders,
  cancelOrder,
  getOrderById,
  listUserOrders,
  placeOrder,
} from "../services/orderService";

export const ordersRouter = Router();
ordersRouter.use(authRequired);

const placeOrderSchema = z.object({
  market: z.string().min(1),
  side: z.enum(["buy", "sell"]),
  orderType: z.enum(["market", "limit"]),
  price: z.string().regex(/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/).optional(),
  quantity: z.string().regex(/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/),
  timeInForce: z.enum(["GTC", "IOC", "FOK"]).optional(),
  leverage: z.string().regex(/^\d+(\.\d+)?$/).optional(),
  marginMode: z.enum(["isolated", "cross"]).optional(),
  reduceOnly: z.boolean().optional(),
  postOnly: z.boolean().optional(),
  clientOrderId: z.string().min(1).max(128).optional(),
});

ordersRouter.post("/", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!req.user) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "unauthorized" });
    return;
  }
  const parsed = placeOrderSchema.safeParse(req.body);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    res.status(400).json({ error: "validation_error", issues: parsed.error.issues });
    return;
  }
  try {
    const result = await placeOrder({ ...parsed.data, userId: req.user.userId });
    res.status(result.idempotent ? 200 : 201).json(result);
  } catch (e: unknown) {
    const err = e as { status?: number; message?: string };
    res.status(err.status ?? 500).json({ error: err.message ?? "internal_error" });
  }
});

ordersRouter.get("/", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!req.user) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "unauthorized" });
    return;
  }
  const status = req.query.status as string | undefined;
  const market = req.query.market as string | undefined;
  const limit = parseInt((req.query.limit as string) || "100", 10);
  const rows = await listUserOrders(req.user.userId, { status, market, limit });
  res.json({ orders: rows });
});

ordersRouter.get("/:id", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!req.user) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "unauthorized" });
    return;
  }
  const order = await getOrderById(String(req.params.id), req.user.userId);
  if (!order) {
    res.status(404).json({ error: "not_found" });
    return;
  }
  res.json(order);
});

ordersRouter.delete("/:id", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!req.user) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "unauthorized" });
    return;
  }
  try {
    const result = await cancelOrder(String(req.params.id), req.user.userId);
    res.json(result);
  } catch (e: unknown) {
    const err = e as { status?: number; message?: string };
    res.status(err.status ?? 500).json({ error: err.message ?? "internal_error" });
  }
});

ordersRouter.delete("/", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!req.user) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "unauthorized" });
    return;
  }
  const market = req.query.market as string | undefined;
  const result = await cancelAllOpenOrders(req.user.userId, market);
  res.json(result);

<file path="Server/src/routes/positions.ts">
import { Router, Request, Response } from "express";
import { and, desc, eq, inArray } from "drizzle-orm";
import { v4 as uuidv4 } from "uuid";
import { db } from "../db/client";
import { assets, markets, orders, positions } from "../db/schema";
import { authRequired } from "../middleware/auth";
import { lockBalance } from "../services/balanceService";
import { D, mul } from "../utils/decimal";
import { REDIS_ORDER_COMMANDS_STREAM, redis } from "../redis";

export const positionsRouter = Router();
positionsRouter.use(authRequired);

positionsRouter.get("/", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!req.user) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "unauthorized" });
    return;
  }
  const status = (req.query.status as string) || "open";
  const rows = await db
    .select()
    .from(positions)
    .where(and(eq(positions.userId, req.user.userId), eq(positions.status, status as "open" | "closed" | "liquidated")))
    .orderBy(desc(positions.openedAt));
  res.json({ positions: rows });
});

positionsRouter.get("/:id", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!req.user) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "unauthorized" });
    return;
  }
  const [row] = await db
    .select()
    .from(positions)
    .where(and(eq(positions.id, String(req.params.id)), eq(positions.userId, req.user.userId)))
    .limit(1);
  if (!row) {
    res.status(404).json({ error: "not_found" });
    return;
  }
  res.json(row);
});

positionsRouter.post("/:id/close", async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
  if (!req.user) {
    res.status(401).json({ error: "unauthorized" });
    return;
  }
  const [pos] = await db
    .select()
    .from(positions)
    .where(and(eq(positions.id, String(req.params.id)), eq(positions.userId, req.user.userId)))
    .limit(1);
  if (!pos) {
    res.status(404).json({ error: "not_found" });
    return;
  }
  if (pos.status !== "open") {
    res.status(400).json({ error: "position_not_open" });
    return;
  }
  const [market] = await db
    .select()
    .from(markets)
    .where(eq(markets.id, pos.marketId))
    .limit(1);
  if (!market) {
    res.status(404).json({ error: "market_not_found" });
    return;
  }
  const closeSide = pos.side === "long" ? "sell" : "buy";
  const orderId = uuidv4();
  const [order] = await db
    .insert(orders)
    .values({
      id: orderId,
      userId: req.user.userId,
      marketId: market.id,
      orderType: "market",
      side: closeSide,
      price: null,
      quantity: pos.quantity,
      filledQuantity: "0",
      status: "open",
      reduceOnly: true,
      postOnly: false,
      timeInForce: "GTC",
      leverage: "1",
      marginMode: pos.marginMode,
    })
    .returning();
  if (!order) {
    res.status(500).json({ error: "order_create_failed" });
    return;
  }
  await redis.xadd(
    REDIS_ORDER_COMMANDS_STREAM,
    "*",
    "type",
    "PLACE_ORDER",
    "orderId",
    orderId,
    "userId",
    req.user.userId,
    "market",
    market.symbol,
    "side",
    closeSide,
    "orderType",
    "market",
    "quantity",
    pos.quantity,
    "timeInForce",
    "GTC",
    "reduceOnly",
    "true",
    "postOnly",
    "false",
    "leverage",
    "1",
    "marginMode",
    pos.marginMode
  );
  res.json({ order });
});

<file path="Server/src/services/authService.ts">
import bcrypt from "bcrypt";
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import { db } from "../db/client";
import { users } from "../db/schema";
import { signToken } from "../middleware/auth";

export async function registerUser(input: {
  email: string;
  password: string;
  name: string;
}): Promise<{ token: string; user: { id: string; email: string; name: string; role: string } }> {
  const existing = await db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.email, input.email)).limit(1);
  if (existing.length > 0) {
    throw Object.assign(new Error("email_already_registered"), { status: 409 });
  }
  const passwordHash = await bcrypt.hash(input.password, 10);
  const [row] = await db
    .insert(users)
    .values({
      email: input.email,
      passwordHash,
      name: input.name,
    })
    .returning();
  if (!row) throw new Error("registration_failed");
  const token = signToken({ userId: row.id, email: row.email, role: row.role });
  return {
    token,
    user: { id: row.id, email: row.email, name: row.name, role: row.role },
  };
}

export async function loginUser(input: {
  email: string;
  password: string;
}): Promise<{ token: string; user: { id: string; email: string; name: string; role: string } }> {
  const [row] = await db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.email, input.email)).limit(1);
  if (!row) {
    throw Object.assign(new Error("invalid_credentials"), { status: 401 });
  }
  const ok = await bcrypt.compare(input.password, row.passwordHash);
  if (!ok) {
    throw Object.assign(new Error("invalid_credentials"), { status: 401 });
  }
  if (!row.tradingEnabled) {
    throw Object.assign(new Error("trading_disabled"), { status: 403 });
  }
  await db
    .update(users)
    .set({ lastLoginAt: new Date(), updatedAt: new Date() })
    .where(eq(users.id, row.id));
  const token = signToken({ userId: row.id, email: row.email, role: row.role });
  return {
    token,
    user: { id: row.id, email: row.email, name: row.name, role: row.role },
  };
}

export async function getUserById(userId: string) {
  const [row] = await db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.id, userId)).limit(1);
  if (!row) return null;
  return {
    id: row.id,
    email: row.email,
    name: row.name,
    role: row.role,
    kycStatus: row.kycStatus,
    tradingEnabled: row.tradingEnabled,
    createdAt: row.createdAt,
    lastLoginAt: row.lastLoginAt,
  };
}
